headline: INTERVIEW | BILL CYORGAN. VOCALIST FROM THE SMASHING PUMPKINS
content: The singer Billy Cyorgán of the band Smashing Pumpkins spoke with Peru21 before arriving in Lima to perform a concert here on March 17th at the Jockey Club del Perú.  What’s your memory of Peru and what do you expect from this visit? If things go like during my first performance, it would be great. I really enjoyed my trip to Peru back in 2010, especially because of its history. Peru is one of the best countries I’ve visited over the last twenty years due to its culture and rich past.  How do you feel about current rock music? It seems everyone collectively decided that rock cannot advance anymore, hence why now people create similar sounding music. This depresses me, making me want to stop playing altogether since many wish to sound like how we did in the past. These individuals think the nineties were sacred times in music and nothing surpasses those days.  So, do you believe there isn’t any future left for rock music? There’s more business involved regarding album sales these days. Although not seen in the charts, where rock barely makes appearances. Before, groups always fought for the leading spots, yet currently, none does—it almost feels extinct.  Are musicians trying to become more commercial... I see different forces balancing each other, ultimately turning everything pop. Even alternative music sounds pop nowadays.  Then, what could happen within the music industry moving forward? Artistic ambition doesnt seem prevalent today. When listening to Nirvana in 1991, Kurt Cobain was someone who wanted to craft unique music—a pioneer creating something entirely his own. Nowadays, competition revolves around popularity contests. Rock artists aim to gain fame while avoiding negative feedback. Music lacks danger, and audiences aren’t reacting strongly anymore.  Do you mean saying the future looks bleak for rock? Not necessarily dangerous—but electronic might pose greater risks compared to guitars, marking quite a sad state indeed.  Currently working on anything else? Yes, crafting a new album. However, striving to ensure it differs significantly from previous works by the Smashing Pumpkins.
